Based on the screenshots and the provided cshtml grammar, I’ve identified two separate issues in components/prism-cshtml.js:

1. The `stringLike` pattern is too greedy: it begins with `@(?!")`, which causes any standalone `@…` in an HTML attribute value to be treated as a string‐delimiter and breaks the markup grammar.  
2. Razor’s `@helper … { … }` blocks are not recognized by the existing “block” pattern (which handles @{…}, @code{…}, @for (…) {…}, etc.), so `@helper TrialHelper(…) { … }` collapses into a single unhighlighted chunk.

Below are two *SEARCH/REPLACE* patches.  The first one removes the leading `@(?!")` from `stringLike`, so that attribute quotes continue to be parsed as HTML strings, even if they contain `@…`.  The second one injects a dedicated `@helper` case into the Razor “block” alternation, so that helpers get proper C#+HTML highlighting inside.

- Still parse your HTML attributes as HTML strings (even if they contain embedded `@Localize.GetLabelHtml("…")` calls), and
